proof:
The feasible coefficient set is nonempty and closed because each test is linear in the coefficients. Both signs of a constant belong to $T_L$, so all feasible coefficients lie in the simplex of mass $
u(C)$. Minimize $\sum_p m_p\lVert Y_pVert^2$ over this compact set. If a nontrivial combination of distinct positive bases has integer average $r$, move from each input mass the amount $t	heta_p$, where $	heta_p$ is its positive combination coefficient and $t>0$ is small, and place the sum $t$ at $r$. For any $h\in T_L$, Jensen for $h+cL$ and exact $L$-interpolation give $h(Y_r)\ge\sum_p	heta_p h(Y_p)$. Thus every cone test survives. The squared-norm moment strictly decreases by strict convexity, a contradiction. Every lattice point of the hull other than its vertices is a nontrivial combination of distinct positive inputs, so there are no such points, and every positive base is a vertex. Two distinct equal-parity vertices would have an integer midpoint, which is also ruled out.

Both signs of any affine test belong to $T_L$, and both signs of $L$ do as well ($-L+L=0$). They give the matching full affine moments and $\sum_p m_pL(Y_p)=\int L\,d
u=1$. For the minimizing masses, use the finite-source allocation argument in the proof of (5) of 86609687edc6bef4: the compact convex moment image consists of the mass and vector moments of nonnegative allocations of $
u$ summing to one. If the desired $(m_p,m_pY_p)_p$ lay outside this image, its separating affine scores $A_p$ would satisfy $\sum_p m_p A_p(Y_p)>\int\max_p A_p\,d
u$. The cone test $-\max_p A_p$ gives the opposite inequality. The allocated rows therefore exist. Each has $\int L\,d
u_p\le m_pL(Y_p)$ by concavity. Their sum is exactly $\int L\,d
u=1$, so each row has equality.
statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex hull with sampled set $S$ and normalized reciprocal target $\nu=dm/(ML)$ for summed positive fiber volume $dm$ of mass $M$ and positive continuous concave $L$ on $C$. Let $J$ be a finite set of integer bases with one mark $Y_p\in S$ over each $p\in J$. Assume that every positive-weight combination of bases in $J$ with integer average $r$ has $r\in J$, with mark and $L$-value equal to the combinations of the input marks and $L$-values. Set
$$
T_L=\{h\in C(C):h+cL\text{ is concave on }C\text{ for some }c\ge0\}.
$$
If some nonnegative masses $m_p$ satisfy $\sum_p m_p h(Y_p)\ge\int h\,d\nu$ for all $h\in T_L$, then there are such masses with positive support $J_0$ satisfying $\operatorname{conv}J_0\cap\mathbb Z^n=J_0$ and with every point of $J_0$ a vertex of its hull. In particular its bases have distinct parities. The new masses satisfy $\sum_p m_pL(Y_p)=1$ and admit rows with target $\nu$, mass $m_p$, barycenter $Y_p$, and $L$-moment $m_pL(Y_p)$.
title: An empty lattice source hull for a full radial-cone certificate
